proposal.rationale: Asset implementations (openssl-3.5, liboqs-0.16.0) support all three allowlisted profiles. Current profile is tls13-x25519 (classical), which is below the security_floor of hybrid-pqc, so migration is required and the current profile cannot be re-proposed. Among peers, only peer-02 and peer-04 have readiness 'known' and advertise the required capabilities for the PQC-capable profiles (kem:x25519mlkem768 and kem:mlkem768); peer-01 and peer-03 only support kem:x25519 and are not ready for any PQC-capable profile, so they are excluded from this batch (not listed as unresolved since their readiness itself is confirmed 'known', just capability-mismatched with target profiles). Both tls13-hybrid-x25519-mlkem768 and tls13-mlkem768 tie at 2 ready endpoints (the maximum achievable). Per the task's tie-break rule I would normally prefer the higher security class (pqc), but CAB decision 2026-31 in the engineering notes explicitly forbids production use of pure ML-KEM profiles and mandates the hybrid profile for this migration, overriding that preference. tls13-hybrid-x25519-mlkem768 also satisfies the security_floor (hybrid-pqc). Recommend scheduling within the Tuesday 02:00-04:00 UTC change window with 30-minute post-change handshake error monitoring per the change window note.
